Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this — we're finalizing our procurement checklist and need explicit assurances around two related points before legal can sign:

1) Training use: a clear, contractible statement that Redwood does not use FintechCo production content to train or improve models (including fine-tuning, continual learning, or offline model training) for the hosted API.

2) Retention and snapshots: we understand operational telemetry and caches exist, but we need details on:

Attached is our standard security_requirements_20281201.pdf for context.

Hi team — drafting below (first pass) for FintechCo legal and a short ops blurb we can attach. I tried to be explicit and conservative so legal has something to work with.

Proposed contract clause (short):
"Redwood Inference represents and warrants that, other than for customers that explicitly contract for model-training services, Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models; Customer Content will not be included in datasets used for model training or evaluation for any Redwood-hosted models.
Redwood will not transfer Customer Content to third parties for the purpose of model training."

Operational controls summary (attachable):
- Request logs: retained for 30 days by default in hosted environments; access restricted to authorized ops personnel and logged.
- KV/prefix caches: ephemeral in-memory caches; persisted cache snapshots are not written to durable object stores except when necessary for planned maintenance; persisted snapshots (rare) are retained for up to 72 hours and deleted by automated jobs.
- Debug snapshots: created only with an internal ticket and approval for incident investigation; retention limited to 7 days by default unless escalation-approved by Security (audit trail required).
- Backups/replicas: periodic backups are encrypted at rest and retained per the backup policy (default 30 days); backups are excluded from any training pipelines and are access-controlled.
- Exceptions: any retention beyond the default windows requires documented approval and is recorded with JIRA ticket IDs and job run IDs; customers may request evidence of deletion (job run IDs, S3 delete markers, audit logs) subject to NDA.

Evidence we can provide:
- Redacted audit log entries showing delete job run IDs and timestamps.
- Screenshots of retention settings and a sample deletion job run (ops playbook excerpt).
- SOC 2 Type II report reference and internal retention policy excerpt.

Attachments: draft_no_train_clause.docx (docx), evidence_playbook_excerpt.pdf (pdf)

Notes: This is intentionally conservative for hosted API commitments. For Dedicated and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) the controls differ: customers that self-host have full control over backups and retention; we can include an admin controls table in a later doc.

If this reads okay I'll send to Sarah and FintechCo Legal as a formal response.

- Priyom
Sr. Product Counsel

Thanks — quick operational clarifications and a tweak to the proposed wording.

On Fri, Dec 1, 2028 at 3:20 PM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed contract clause (short):
> "Redwood Inference represents and warrants that ... Redwood will not transfer Customer Content to third parties for the purpose of model training."

Technical/ops details to add for completeness:
- Live request logs (signed requests, timestamps, routing metadata): retained in hot storage for 30 days. Cold tier archival backups exist for 90 days for legal/forensics use in hosted environments; archives are strongly access-controlled and never ingested into training pipelines.
- KV/prefix caches: these are in-process LRU caches on GPU hosts; they are normally not materialized. When we flush or snapshot a cache (maintenance, scaling), the snapshot is written to an encrypted ephemeral blob store and is scrubbed by an automated job. Typical snapshot TTL = 72 hours; deletion is performed by object lifecycle jobs which create a delete marker and a run-id we can provide.
- Debug snapshots / reproductions: created only after an internal incident ticket is opened; PR approvals from Security and the Incident Commander are required; retention default 7 days; for critical investigations retention may be extended to 30 days with logged approvals.
- Backups: incremental backups are retained 30 days; full backups are rotated monthly and retained 90 days for hosted accounts. These backups are logically separated from any datasets used for model work and are access controlled via RBAC.

Suggested contractual tweak (to reduce ambiguity):
Add: "For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing does not limit Redwood's ability to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry that cannot be traced to Customer Content nor pre-existing public datasets; such aggregated telemetry will not include Customer Content."

What we can hand over as evidence:
- Example delete job run-id and corresponding audit log entry (redacted).
- A small ops CSV showing snapshot TTLs and deletion timestamps (ops_snapshot_retention.csv).
- SOC 2 Type II reference and the name/contact for the auditor (available under NDA).

I'll sign off on Priyom's draft with the tweaks above and include the three artifacts. Monica, please confirm customer comms readiness and timeline (they need this by Tuesday).

Thanks,
